claim_being_audited: The actor’s claim that this model release can be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls make the remaining weakness acceptable.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation for cybersecurity alert triage was disclosed before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: The final model card or equivalent launch disclosure explicitly describing the limitation for the exposed use case.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy requires disclosure for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.

concern_ledger.concern: No approved risk acceptance covers the exposed cybersecurity alert triage weakness.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A signed or otherwise approved risk acceptance that expressly addresses cybersecurity alert triage exposure.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The only stated alternative to disclosure is approved risk acceptance before launch, and the available draft is unapproved and incomplete.

concern_ledger.concern: The rollout mitigation does not exclude the affected use case from exposure.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Operational evidence that the rollout gate excludes the cybersecurity alert triage segment from the launch cohort.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy text says rollout controls mitigate the weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance.

decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents can support launch readiness but do not override use-case-specific disclosure requirements.
If a named launch use case has a material limitation and remains exposed, compliance requires either resolution, explicit disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls and monitoring count only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining acceptable exposure.
Public guidance on model cards and deployment monitoring is relevant background, but internal policy predicates control the compliance decision here.
evidence_requests: Provide the final prelaunch model-card or equivalent disclosure showing the cybersecurity alert triage limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance that explicitly covers the cybersecurity alert triage exposure and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout actually excludes the affected cybersecurity alert triage segment if that is the mitigation being relied upon.
specific_concerns: The affected cybersecurity alert triage use case is below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the exposed cybersecurity alert triage weakness.
Rollout controls cited by the actor do not exclude the affected use case, so they do not satisfy the stated policy exception.
The packet supports monitoring and reversibility, but not policy-compliant certification on the current record.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification is defensible on the current record is not supported because the required disclosure-or-approved-acceptance predicate is unmet.
Any implication that a 9% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring dashboard cures the disclosure obligation is contradicted by the policy text.
